subject: math

objective.text: Find how much time passes in whole hours and half hours.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective: Solve elapsed time problems involving whole hours and a half hour.

explanations.title: Count the hours
explanations.text: Start at the first time. Count each hour on the clock until you reach the end time.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Problem 2 (S: I counted on the clock)

explanations.title: Crossing noon or midnight
explanations.text: From a.m. to p.m., you cannot just subtract. Count the hours forward past 12.

explanations.title: The arrow way
explanations.text: Hop to midnight first. Then hop to the end time. Add the hops.

explanations.title: Same time, a.m. and p.m.
explanations.text: 8:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. look the same on a clock. They are 12 hours apart.

examples.title: Beth's sleep
examples.text: 8:00 p.m. to midnight is 4 hours. Midnight to 3:30 a.m. is 3 and a half hours. That is 7 and a half hours.

questions.text: What is 600 minus 356?
What is 406 minus 218?
Jean watches cartoons of 14 minutes and 28 minutes. After a 5-minute break, she watches 15 minutes more. How long does she watch cartoons?
Jean may watch for 1 hour. Did she go over her time limit?
Kalpana gets up at 7:00 a.m. She leaves at 7:30 a.m. How long does she take to get ready?

source_ref.section: Concept Development Problem 1 (S: 30 minutes. Half an hour.)

questions.text: Tony goes bowling at 2:00 p.m. He gets home at 9:00 p.m. How long was he out?
Students arrive at the museum at 10:00 a.m. They leave at 2:00 p.m. How long are they there?
A movie starts at 11:30 a.m. It ends at 1:30 p.m. How long is the movie?
Beth goes to bed at 8:00 p.m. She wakes up at 3:30 a.m. How long did she sleep?

source_ref.section: Concept Development Problem 5 (S: Seven and a half hours.)

questions.text: One clock shows 8:00 a.m. Another shows 8:00 p.m. the same day. How much time is between them?
How much time passes from 1:30 p.m. to 4:30 p.m.?

source_ref.section: Concept Development Problem 6 sequence: 4:30 p.m. and 1:30 p.m.

questions.text: How much time passes from 2:30 a.m. to 7:00 a.m.?

source_ref.section: Concept Development Problem 6 sequence: 7:00 a.m. and 2:30 a.m.

questions.text: How much time passes from 6:30 a.m. to 7:00 a.m.?
How much time passes from 11:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.?
How much time passes from 7:00 p.m. to 1:30 a.m.?
Tracy gets to school at 7:30 a.m. She leaves at 3:30 p.m. How long is she at school?
Anna spent 3 hours at dance practice. She finished at 6:15 p.m. What time did she start?
Andy's practice was 2 hours long. It finished at 4:30 p.m. What time did it start?
Marcus drove from 7:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on Monday. On Tuesday he drove from 6:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. How long did he drive in all?
Jamal's picnic started at 1:30 p.m. He stayed 4 and a half hours. What time did he leave?
Tracy arrives and leaves on the half hour. Why isn't she at school 8 and a half hours?

hints.text: Start at the first time. Count each hour on the clock.
Hop to 12 first. Then hop to the end time.
Check the a.m. and p.m. Does it pass noon or midnight?
From :30 to the next o'clock is half an hour.
Count back from the end time.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Problem 3 (S: I went back in time)

hints.text: Add only the cartoon times. Do not add the break.
Subtract the ones, then the tens, then the hundreds.

misconceptions.label: Adding time that is not part of the question
misconceptions.description: Child adds the 5-minute break into Jean's cartoon time, and thinks she broke the time limit.
detection_signals: Says Jean broke her time limit.
misconceptions.response_text: The break is not cartoon time. Add only the 3 cartoons.

source_ref.section: Application Problem note: 'not to add in the 5-minute break'

misconceptions.label: Subtracting clock numbers across noon or midnight
misconceptions.description: Child subtracts the hour numbers when the times go from a.m. to p.m. (for example 11:30 to 1:30 gives 10).
detection_signals: Says 10 hours for 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m.
Gives a very large answer for a short time that crosses 12.
misconceptions.response_text: We go past 12, so we cannot just subtract. Count the hours forward on the clock.

assets_required.why_this_method: Hand positions must be exact, and the hour hand must move partway between numbers. Diffusion cannot do this.
assets_required.description: An analog clock with numbers 1-12, minute marks, an hour hand and a minute hand. Can also show a digital readout.
must_show_exactly: Numbers 1-12 in correct positions, 60 minute marks
Minute hand points exactly at the stimulus minute
Hour hand sits between hours in proportion to the minutes (for example halfway between 3 and 4 at 3:30)
Two clocks side by side for start and end times, each with a.m. or p.m. label
states_or_frames: any time hh:mm from the stimulus
minute hand moving from start to end
assets_required.interaction: Display, or the child drags the hands. The tutor sets the time from the question stimulus.
assets_required.alt_text: A clock face with an hour hand and a minute hand.
assets_required.generation_caption: Clean flat analog clock face, numbers 1 to 12, two hands, plain white background, no text. [Build by code]

assets_required.why_this_method: Hops must be exact hours and half hours between labelled times.
assets_required.description: The 'arrow way': a start time, hops of 1 hour (or a half hour), and an end time. Can pass through 12:00 noon or midnight.
must_show_exactly: Each full hop = 1 hour; half hop = 30 minutes
Noon and midnight marked when crossed
Hop count equals the answer key
states_or_frames: 8:00 p.m. -> 12:00 a.m. (4 hops) -> 3:30 a.m. (3 and a half hops)
assets_required.interaction: Tap to add a hop; the tool shows the time after each hop.
assets_required.alt_text: Hops from a start time to an end time.
assets_required.generation_caption: Simple horizontal arrow with curved hop arrows above, flat style. [Build by code]

assets_required.description: A row of boxes: cartoon 14 minutes, cartoon 28 minutes, break 5 minutes, cartoon 15 minutes; a 1-hour limit line.
assets_required.alt_text: A timeline of cartoons and a break.
assets_required.generation_caption: Simple row of TV-screen icons with time labels, flat style. [Build by code]

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.

Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
